rv.q: If you like wartime stories, James Bond movies and appreciate goofiness, “Operation Mincemeat” will make for a very juicy night out.
"Operation Mincemeat" is amazingly well conceived as a stage spectacle.
Operation Mincemeat is an absolute smash.
This is among the best shows out there right now, and one that will stay with me for a long time.
“Operation Mincemeat” feels much broader and more complex than you may think that the modest-in-numbers ensemble might be capable of delivering.
The show succeeds at taking a serious subject, World War Two, and finding the comedy in the outrageous scheme to fool Hitler and win the war.
You won’t soon forget this musical, and that can’t be said about quite a few of the other offerings at PPAC this season.
A corpse, a preposterous plan, and five tireless performers make this British spy caper an enormously funny exercise in controlled chaos.
But this touring production feels like a copy of a copy: louder, broader, and far less able to carry the weight of its own concept.

cn.t: Critics hail this irreverent British WWII musical as inventive and enormously funny, praising its original approach to an improbable true story and tireless five-person cast, though a few find the controlled chaos doesn't fully land.
